question: A GPU box is Windows 11 and IT will not enable WSL or Hyper-V containers. Plan a native model action without running anything.
ground_truth: Select tao-run-on-windows-venv as the native Windows, no-WSL, no-container execution platform. First read and run the selected model's Windows preflight, then open a windows-venv job record, submit its module/script/entrypoint through windows_job_runner.py, poll status and logs, cancel with the runner if needed, and mark the record after a terminal state.
expected_behavior: Identifies tao-run-on-windows-venv as the relevant platform
Requires the selected model's preflight before launch
Uses record-then-launch and the four verbs over windows_job_runner.py
Uses exactly one model-provided script, module, or entrypoint selector
Does not run commands, scripts, or web searches

question: A model explicitly supports native Windows ARM64 and requires 72 GiB of CUDA capacity. Describe the platform checks without executing them.
ground_truth: Use the target venv interpreter, verify that platform.machine is ARM64 and that CUDA is visible, then run the explicit 72 GiB allocation probe. The probe writes and synchronizes a CUDA uint8 allocation before freeing it. It does not reserve memory or prove the model package, ABI, decoder, or workload fit; those remain model-skill checks.
expected_behavior: Requires native ARM64 Python rather than emulated AMD64
Uses the explicit allocation probe rather than only torch.cuda.is_available
Explains that the probe frees memory and is not a reservation
Keeps model ABI and workload validation with the selected model skill

question: Explain how the native Windows runner decides whether a submitted job is still alive and why it does not use os.kill(pid, 0). Do not run anything.
ground_truth: Liveness uses OpenProcess with SYNCHRONIZE and PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION followed by WaitForSingleObject(handle, 0). The runner avoids os.kill(pid, 0) because Windows CPython does not implement a signal-zero probe and can terminate the target instead. A named Job Object and GetProcessTimes creation time make the durable identity safe against PID reuse.
expected_behavior: Names WaitForSingleObject with a zero timeout as the liveness probe
Explains that os.kill on Windows can terminate instead of probe
Mentions the named Job Object or GetProcessTimes creation time
Does not run commands, scripts, or web searches
